messages:
Elliot (SE): Heads up — NexaMed POC streaming is intermittently stalling when they go through their corp proxy. Python client starts streaming then hangs; no exception. Anyone seen this pattern with proxy auth/inspector?
Maya (AE): They're on the call now, said it works if they bypass the proxy. On proxy it stalls after ~12-18s.
Jon (Solutions): Do we have client logs or gateway traces? trace id?
Elliot (SE): Client shows keepalive but no payload, code snippet below (python):
```py
resp = client.stream_responses(model='redwood-8k', input=prompt)
for chunk in resp:
    print('chunk', chunk.text)
```
Python 3.11, @redwood/py 1.2.0
Rana (Eng): 1.2.0 had small changes to chunk flush. Are they using an outbound proxy that requires NTLM or proxy-auth? Those often buffer until full or after auth handshake.
Elliot (SE): Proxy does header-based auth with an inline appliance (not NTLM). They also have an inline DLP that re-signs TLS certs.
Jon (Solutions): Inline TLS re-signing + auth headers could cause two problems: (A) inspector buffers small chunks until a threshold, (B) proxy closes idle upstreams if it doesn't see activity post-auth.
Elliot (SE): Runtime logs show repeated 502/503 and occasional 401 from upstream before success: [2026-03-01T09:33:20Z] WARN gw: upstream 401 trace=tr-ff12a9 headers={"connection":"keep-alive"}
Maya (AE): NexaMed asked about Private deployment / VPC options because of this — they want to avoid inline inspection. Also asked for monthly commit pricing for 2 A100 nodes. I'll need a quote.
Rana (Eng): Quick triage: (1) increase client-side chunk size or ensure flush on each chunk, (2) add send-side heartbeat frames / nop bytes every 8s, (3) bump HTTP header size if the proxy squeezes headers. On Python SDK we have `client.stream_responses(..., chunk_size=...)` and a streaming helper to send pings.
Elliot (SE): Trying (2) + upgrade to py 1.2.3 (contains heartbeat helper). Sending sample patch:
```py
from threading import Timer
stream = client.stream_responses(...)
def ping():
    client._send_heartbeat()
    Timer(8.0, ping).start()
ping()
for c in stream:
    print(c.text)
```
Jon (Solutions): Also ask NexaMed infra to check 'inspect-buffer-limit' and 'idle-reassembly-timeout' on their appliance.
Elliot (SE): After enabling heartbeat + upgrade to 1.2.3, streaming ran for 25m without stall, then a 30s gap, then resumed. Logs attached.
Rana (Eng): That matches inspector buffering then doing a TLS renegotiation/close. I'll open RT-4010 to add an explicit heartbeat option to the Python SDK and doc recommendation for proxies.
Maya (AE): I'll attach Private deployment pricing and the security questionnaire answers. They also asked about SAML metadata, SCIM provisioning, and whether we support customer-managed keys. I confirmed SAML, SCIM and KMS/HSM support in Private.
Elliot (SE): NexaMed security team still wants to confirm whether our runtime will run in their VPC for PII-handling endpoints. I offered a short proof-of-concept in our Private eval environment.
Jon (Solutions): Next actions: (A) Maya send 2-A100 monthly commit quote, (B) Rana open SDK ticket RT-4010, (C) Nexa infra to provide appliance buffer settings, (D) Elliot run a controlled test bypassing proxy and then reintroducing it with heartbeat.
infra-bot: Ticket RT-4010 created by Rana: "python sdk: add streaming heartbeat option + docs" assigned to eng-runtime. ETA 6d.
Elliot (SE): Quick update 1m later: full successful test bypassing proxy. With proxy + heartbeat it was stable for 40m in one trial. Will schedule longer soak.
Maya (AE): Quote sent. They want a follow-up demo of Private deployment next Tue.
Rana (Eng): I'll PR a small sample in the SDK repo showing heartbeat usage and a short blurb in streaming docs.
Elliot (SE): Thanks team 44D will re-open thread if this flares up again.
